# recommend_all

Batch collaborative-filtering recommender. Consumes a whole relation of `(user, item, value)` interactions, fits an implicit-feedback Alternating Least Squares (ALS) model over the entire user x item matrix, and returns the **top-N recommended items for every user** that appears in the input.

## When to use
Use this when you want personalized recommendations for the full user base in one pass -- e.g. precomputing a 'recommended for you' shelf for every user. For a single user prefer `recommend_for`; for item-to-item neighbours prefer `similar_items`.

## Inputs
- `Arg(0)`: a `(SELECT user, item, value)` subquery -- the interaction relation.
- `user`, `item`, `value`: names of the columns playing each role.
- `n`: recommendations per user (default 10).
- `factors`: ALS latent-factor count (default 50, clamped on tiny matrices).

## Output
Rows of `(user, item, score, rank)`; `score` is the ALS dot-product score and `rank` is 1-based within each user (1 = best).

## Behavior & edge cases
Items the user has already interacted with are excluded. `value` is the interaction confidence and defaults to 1.0 when the value column is absent. Results are deterministic (pinned random_state, single-threaded BLAS).

## recommend_all

Top-N collaborative-filtering recommendations for **all** users, computed with implicit-feedback ALS over the supplied interaction relation.

### Usage

Pass the interaction relation as the positional `(user, item, value)` subquery and name the role columns plus `n` (recommendations per user). Each output row is `(user, item, score, rank)`; order by `user` then `rank` for a stable, per-user ranked list. A ready-to-run demonstration lives in this function's example queries.

### Notes

- One ALS model is fit over the entire matrix, so the whole relation is buffered before any rows are emitted.
- Already-seen items are never recommended back to a user.
- `value` (confidence) defaults to 1.0 if the column is missing; `factors` is auto-clamped on small matrices.

# recommend_for

Single-user collaborative-filtering recommender. Fits implicit-feedback ALS over the supplied `(user, item, value)` interaction relation and returns the **top-N recommended items for one target user** (`target_user`, a named scalar argument), excluding items that user has already interacted with.

## When to use
Use this for an on-demand 'recommended for you' list for a specific user. For the whole user base in one pass use `recommend_all`; for item-to-item neighbours use `similar_items`.

## Inputs
- `Arg(0)`: a `(SELECT user, item, value)` subquery -- the interaction relation.
- `user`, `item`, `value`: names of the columns playing each role.
- `target_user`: the id of the single user to recommend for (named scalar).
- `n`: number of recommendations (default 10).
- `factors`: ALS latent-factor count (default 50, clamped on tiny matrices).

## Output
Rows of `(item, score, rank)`; `score` is the ALS dot-product score and `rank` is 1-based (1 = best).

## Behavior & edge cases
An unknown `target_user` yields zero rows (not an error). Already-seen items are excluded. `value` is interaction confidence and defaults to 1.0 when absent. Deterministic (pinned random_state, single-threaded BLAS).

## recommend_for

Top-N collaborative-filtering recommendations for a **single target user**, computed with implicit-feedback ALS over the supplied interaction relation.

### Usage

Pass the interaction relation as the positional `(user, item, value)` subquery, name the role columns, and set `target_user` to the id of the one user to score (plus `n`, the number of recommendations). Each output row is `(item, score, rank)`, ordered by `rank`. A ready-to-run demonstration lives in this function's example queries.

### Notes

- `target_user` is a named scalar argument naming the one user to score.
- An unknown `target_user` returns an empty result rather than raising.
- Already-seen items are never recommended; `value` (confidence) defaults to 1.0 if the column is missing.

# similar_items

Item-to-item collaborative-filtering neighbour finder. Fits implicit-feedback ALS over the supplied `(user, item, value)` interaction relation, then for **every item** returns its top-N most similar items ranked by the cosine similarity of their ALS latent factors.

## When to use
Use this to power 'customers who liked X also liked Y', 'related products', or 'more like this' surfaces -- recommendations that depend on an item, not a user. For per-user recommendations use `recommend_all` or `recommend_for`.

## Inputs
- `Arg(0)`: a `(SELECT user, item, value)` subquery -- the interaction relation.
- `user`, `item`, `value`: names of the columns playing each role.
- `n`: similar items per item (default 10).
- `factors`: ALS latent-factor count (default 50, clamped on tiny matrices).

## Output
Rows of `(item, similar_item, similarity, rank)`; `similarity` is cosine of the ALS item factors (1.0 = identical) and `rank` is 1-based per item.

## Behavior & edge cases
An item is never listed as its own neighbour (the self-match at similarity 1.0 is dropped). `value` is interaction confidence and defaults to 1.0 when absent. Items co-interacted by the same users score as nearest neighbours. Deterministic (pinned random_state, single-threaded BLAS).

## similar_items

Top-N most **similar items** for every item, by cosine similarity of implicit-feedback ALS item factors over the supplied interaction relation.

### Usage

Pass the interaction relation as the positional `(user, item, value)` subquery and name the role columns plus `n` (neighbours per item). Each output row is `(item, similar_item, similarity, rank)`; order by `item` then `rank` for a stable neighbour list. A ready-to-run demonstration lives in this function's example queries.

### Notes

- The query item itself is excluded from its own neighbour list.
- One ALS model is fit over the whole matrix, so the relation is fully buffered before any rows are emitted.
- `value` (confidence) defaults to 1.0 if the column is missing; `factors` is auto-clamped on small matrices.
